note: Round-4 additions: pharmaceutical PATENTS only. Same schema as pdf_corpus_round3_manifest.json. source_url is provenance, not a required fetch - the PDFs are committed under benchmarks/corpus/ with SHA256SUMS. n_expected counts the NAMED molecules the document draws that were catalogued, including any listed under drawn_but_not_scored; n_resolved counts those carrying a PubChem CID. est_structures is the total number of DRAWINGS on the page and is much larger. Every CID here was resolved from the printed CAS or IUPAC name and then CHECKED against the drawing; four lookups returned a plausible but WRONG compound and are flagged in the note field of the molecule concerned.
retrieval_note: The round-1..3 retrieval route (fetch patents.google.com/patent/<ID>/en and read <meta name=citation_pdf_url>) now returns HTTP 503 "your computer or network may be sending automated queries" from this box. Two routes that do work: (a) for US documents, https://patentimages.storage.googleapis.com/pdfs/US<number>.pdf with no kind code and no hash - 200 application/octet-stream, real %PDF-, recorded as 403 in round 1 and it is not, at least for US; (b) for any country, resolve the hashed patentimages path through a server-side fetcher rather than curl, then curl the hashed URL directly, which is not blocked. https://data.epo.org/publication-server/rest/v1.2/patents/EP<number>NW<kind>/document.pdf also serves EP documents unauthenticated with no publication date in the path, and /rest/v1.2/publication-dates/<YYYYMMDD>/patents lists every document published on a date.

accepted.drawing_style: USPTO scan, 300-dpi CCITT full-page raster. A style the corpus does not otherwise have: SEMI-CONDENSED 1980s patent art - ring systems drawn as skeletons but side chains written as inline text on the bond (`CH2CH2CH2N(CH3)2`, `CH2OH`, `OCH3`), reagents drawn with every atom spelled out (`KO-C(CH3)3`, `CH3-SO2-Cl`), and enantiomers distinguished by a printed (+) or (-) beside the drawing
accepted.structure_pages: p1 abstract structure (citalopram, formula I); p2 formula I and the diol formula II; p3 REACTION SCHEME I (the diol, both Mosher acid chlorides, both diastereomeric esters, potassium tert-butoxide, and the (+) and (-) enantiomers of citalopram drawn separately) plus the start of REACTION SCHEME II (diol + methanesulfonyl chloride); p4 Scheme II continued (the mesylate, NEt3); p5 Example structures; p7 formula II redrawn with a generic ester R. Text-only p6 and pp8-9 (two Certificates of Correction)
accepted.why: A resolution patent that draws BOTH enantiomers of the same 2D skeleton, with the configuration carried only by a printed (+)/(-) and the wedge on the quaternary carbon - the sharpest stereo-discrimination test in the corpus, and the counterpart to the salt tests. It is also a deliberate HARD POSITIVE for depiction style: the side chains are written as condensed text rather than drawn, which is the style round two rejected US3385886A ibuprofen for. Expect low recall here; that is the measurement. Nine pages cost almost nothing, and it pairs with DE60100786T2 - same molecule, same applicant, different language and PDF class

accepted.title: US 8,524,733 B2, Gant and Shahbaz, Auspex Pharmaceuticals, granted 2013-09-03, "Benzoquinoline inhibitors of vesicular monoamine transporter 2" (the deutetrabenazine / Austedo patent)
accepted.drawing_style: USPTO scan, 300-dpi CCITT full-page raster. ChemDraw line art in which DEUTERIUM is drawn as an explicit `D` atom label on each substituted position - typically 6 to 17 D labels crowded onto one roughly 1150x400 px depiction
accepted.structure_pages: p1 abstract Markush formula I (R1-R23); p3 tetrabenazine drawn specific and labelled; p4 Markush formula I again; pp11-12 Schemes I and II, R-substituted (generic); p13 Example 1, the non-deuterated route (dihydroisoquinoline, the quaternary ammonium iodide, tetrabenazine); pp13-14 Example 2, the SAME route run with CD3I (d6-nitrovinyl catechol, d6-homoveratrylamine, d6-dihydroisoquinoline, deutetrabenazine); pp15-26 a gallery of about 140 explicitly deuterated analogues, roughly 12 per page; p27 the claim-1 structure. Text-only pp2 and 5-10
accepted.why: The ONLY isotopically labelled document available, and it tests a recognition mode nothing else in the corpus does: reading a `D` atom label as deuterium rather than as a generic substituent or an R-group. Examples 1 and 2 are the same synthesis run with CH3I and with CD3I, giving a controlled isotope pair on an identical skeleton. It is NOT Markush-free - formula I appears twice and Schemes I/II are generic - but that is 4 generic drawings against roughly 150 committed ones. Expect the gallery compounds to be unscoreable (hypothetical analogues absent from PubChem); that is the same accepted outcome as the macrocycle paper's Boc/Fmoc intermediates

accepted.title: US 4,117,118, Haerri, Ruegger, Dreyfuss and Kobel, Sandoz Ltd., granted 1978-09-26, "Organic compounds" (the original cyclosporin A / S 7481/F-1 isolation patent)
accepted.drawing_style: 1978 typeset and hand-inked line art scanned at 300 dpi CCITT. A style nothing else in the corpus has: a fully condensed peptide backbone with every atom spelled out (CH3, CH2, CH, N, CO), STEREOCHEMISTRY CARRIED BY PRINTED LETTERS - a D, L or R beside each alpha carbon instead of a wedge - and dotted lines for intramolecular hydrogen bonds
accepted.structure_pages: pp2-7 are FIG 1-6, the UV, IR and 90 MHz 1H NMR spectra of S 7481/F-1 and F-2 - six NON-STRUCTURE figures; p8 the complete structure of S 7481/F-1 (cyclosporin A) as a cyclic undecapeptide; p9 the complete structure of S 7481/F-2. Text-only p1 and pp10-17
accepted.why: Two things nothing else in the corpus provides. (1) SIZE: cyclosporin A is 85 heavy atoms drawn as one connected object filling half a page - by far the largest single depiction in the corpus, and a direct test of whether the segmenter emits it as one structure or several. (2) STEREO AS TEXT: the D/L/R letters are the only configuration information in the drawing, and the R letters are an excellent trap, since an OCSR tool has every reason to read `R` as an R-group. It is also the round's only pre-1980 document, and the six spectra give it six built-in negatives

expected_molecules.note: VERIFIED FROM THE DRAWING, not from the text: at 300 dpi the residue between MeBmt and sarcosine carries a CH2-CH3 side chain, i.e. 2-aminobutyric acid, which is cyclosporin A's residue 2

drawn_but_not_scored.name: S 7481/F-2, named cyclosporin B in the text
drawn_but_not_scored.reason: EXCLUDED FROM THE DENOMINATOR on purpose. The document names F-2 as cyclosporin B ([Ala2]cyclosporin A), but at 300 dpi its residue-2 side chain reads as CH2-CH3 (Abu), the same as the F-1 drawing, and the empirical formula the document prints for F-1, C61H109N11O12, is PubChem's formula for cyclosporin B (CID 12797522) rather than for cyclosporin A (C62H111N11O12, CID 5284373). Two identity signals inside the same document disagree, so neither is trusted for scoring. Anyone wanting this drawing scored should settle A vs B against the 1976 Helv. Chim. Acta papers the patent cites
